quarterly_data.signal: AstraZeneca entered into a clinical collaboration agreement with Summit Therapeutics to evaluate sonesitatug vedotin (Sone-Ve, its CLDN18.2-targeting MMAE ADC) in combination with Summit's ivonescimab (a PD-1/VEGF bispecific engineered by Akeso; Summit holds rights in major territories outside China) in gastrointestinal cancers; the companies intend to initiate trials under the collaboration imminently. Each company contributes its own medicine, the two jointly contribute to trial costs, and each retains development and commercial rights to its medicine. The companies also executed an MOU with the intent to enter an agreement initiating a global development programme combining ivonescimab with AstraZeneca's cancer medicines, including additional ADCs, alongside AstraZeneca's equity investment in Summit. Ivonescimab is approved in China for certain NSCLC patients and a BLA in EGFR-mutated NSCLC is under FDA review. Susan Galbraith (EVP, Oncology Haematology R&D): broadening the reach of the ADC portfolio as the backbone of treatment, with combinations alongside next-generation immunotherapies, is a core pillar of the oncology strategy.
